english.title: Person other than maker carry out activities under unregistered foreign influence arrangement
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person who

(A)_[held office in or under]_
(B)_[was an employee or other member of staff of]_

a foreign power specified by the Secretary of State in regulations **(..SPECIFY FOREIGN POWER..), carried out a political influence activity namely **(..SPECIFY ACTIVITY..), in the UK in that capacity, having made a misrepresentation about your activities or the capacity in which you acted when that activity was not registered with the Secretary of State by that person
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 71(3) and 80(3) of the National Security Act 2023.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
after the end of the registration period under section 69 of the National Security Act 2023
carried out a political influence activity OR
arranged for a political influence activity to be carried out in the United Kingdom
pursuant to an unregistered foreign influence arrangement made by another
knowing or, having regard to other matters known, you ought reasonably to have known, that you were acting pursuant to a foreign influence arrangement

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See the offence under sections 69(5) at H101467, which relates to failure to comply with registration requirements and should also be considered in cases where this offence has been committed.
(ii) A defence is available to a person who has taken all steps reasonably practicable to determine whether the activities in question are or are not registered, and having taken such steps, reasonably believes that they are registered (sections 71(5)).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or fine.
Indictment : maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
